angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 208,710 km at 18.55 pc = 0.15 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 53.8975 +/- 0.0268 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 18.55 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Poultourtzidis et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5388.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract): 208,710 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.292 +/- 0.018 solar masses from Poultourtzidis et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5388.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3440 +/- 85 K from Poultourtzidis et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5388.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Poultourtzidis et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5388.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...707A.106P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5388.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.949, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
